concerns.text: Utility is modeled with a Gaussian GLMM despite being a binary per‑episode outcome. This violates construct validity; a binomial/logistic GLMM (or proportion‑based model) should be used.

The intent classifier repurposes a sentiment‑trained DistilBERT model for intent detection without validation of mapping accuracy, threatening construct validity of the Access Control and Forgetting metrics.

Power analysis assumes a medium effect size (Cohen’s h ≈ 0.3) uniformly across binary and continuous metrics, but does not justify this for each metric nor account for the Holm‑Bonferroni correction’s impact on required sample size.

Fallback to alternative tests (McNemar, paired t‑test, Wilcoxon) is described only as a contingency, without pre‑specifying which test will be used if assumptions fail, risking post‑hoc selection bias.
Domain is treated as a fixed effect with only four levels; this may not adequately control for within‑domain variability and could confound the method effect.
